summary: Thousand Islands light whose iron tower was raised in 1894 and moved onto a brick base in 1903; the 1889 Vickery wreck; a keeper's widow who served in 1901.

light.characteristic_note: Lantern on dwelling 1848; later white then red (red from 10 April 1904, LighthouseFriends); Rowlett gives 'continuous white light' for the 1882 tower

structures.note: One-and-a-half-story brick dwelling with a lantern on the pitched roof (LighthouseFriends)
Detached iron tower on a concrete pad (LighthouseFriends; Rowlett 1882)
Old iron tower set atop a new conical brick base; LighthouseFriends describes a fifty-foot tower joined by a walkway

Two-story, eight-room Victorian dwelling (LighthouseFriends: begun May 1884, completed August 1884). Rowlett gives two-story frame keeper's quarters dated 1882; the USLHS record gives a Victorian wood dwelling dated 1848. Not resolved.

staffing.note: Last principal keeper on the roster 1955-1956

access.note: State park, reached by boat only. Lighthouse and keeper's quarters open from 15 May to 19 September, 10 a.m. to 5 p.m.; the lighthouse closed for the season on the park page.

facts.agency: New York State Parks (LighthouseFriends); New York State Office of Parks, Recreation and Historic Preservation (USLHS)

events.note: Congress appropriates $6,000 for three Thousand Islands lights on 3 March 1847
Government buys Rock Island, Crossover Island and Sunken Rock from their owners for $250 in April 1847
One-and-a-half-story brick dwelling with lantern built (LighthouseFriends)
First keeper appointed 15 May 1848 (LighthouseFriends); USLHS gives station established 1848; Rowlett gives 1847
Lantern refitted with a sixth-order Fresnel lens (LighthouseFriends)
Light-House Board says a new tower is imperatively necessary; $14,000 needed (quoted by LighthouseFriends)
Detached iron tower erected on a concrete pad
Two-story Victorian dwelling begun May 1884, completed August 1884
Schooner Vickery runs aground near the lighthouse on 15 August 1889; crew spend the night at the station
Tribune dispatch dated 23 August 1889 from Thousand Island Park: the side-wheel steamer Sport ran into the wrecked schooner Vickery one night; the OCR text gives no location

Tower raised bodily 5 ft, with a solid octagonal wall of red granite under it (Board report for the year ended 30 June 1895, entry 1076); small light discontinued in 1894 at the close of navigation; LighthouseFriends dates the work to fall 1894
Keeper Michael Diepolder dies on 16 July 1901; Emma Diepolder serves until September (roster: laborer; LighthouseFriends: keeper)
Old iron tower set on a new conical brick base near the north side of the island
Light changed from white to red on 10 April 1904; about then a fourth-order Fresnel lens installed
On 9 May, during a gale, keeper John C. Belden rescues five men from a disabled power boat drifting across the shoals (Lighthouse Service Bulletin 1915 volume)
Light inactive from 1956 (Rowlett: inactive 1956-2013); last principal keeper on the roster 1955-1956; LighthouseFriends says the last keeper left in December 1956
NPGallery record dated 14 November 1978 (date published); the sources read give no separate listing date
Rock Island Lighthouse Historical and Memorial Association formed
Restoration begins June 2010 at $1.1 million (Rowlett); LighthouseFriends says $1.5 million in federal and state funds. The sources differ
Restoration completed early 2013 and lighthouse opened for tours in June (Rowlett); LighthouseFriends says state parks unveiled the island to the public on 4 June 2013

corrections.proposed: cast-iron tower built 1882; 1848 structure was the lantern on the brick dwelling
corrections.why: LighthouseFriends and Rowlett date the detached iron tower to 1882; the 1848 station was a lantern on the keeper's dwelling. The 1903 brick base carried the iron tower.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Rowlett gives 1847 (establishment); USLHS gives 1848. LighthouseFriends says the dwelling was built in 1847 and the first keeper appointed 15 May 1848, so the story uses 1848 for the first keeper and light.

notes_for_editor: Checked 2026-10-22 against: the LighthouseFriends page (ID 317); the USLHS place record (rock-island); the Light-House Board report for the year ended 30 June 1895 (corpus, entry 1076 on scan p.357, printed p.142 confirmed from the running header); the New-York Tribune of 23 August 1889, p.7 (OCR; the 'Sport' name and the 'A YACHT RUNS INTO A WRECK' heading read; the OCR does not show 'off Rock Island Light', so no location is given); the Lighthouse Service Bulletin 1915 (PDF p.23, Belden rescue confirmed; the OCR drops the distance, so the story says 'some distance'); Rowlett's Rock Island entry; the NPGallery asset page 78001855 (Date Published 11/14/1978); and the NYS Parks page (hours, keeper's quarters, lantern room, Clayton Island Tours, 'closed for the season'). NRHP nomination PDF for 78001855 is not digitised in our cache (placeholder); only the NPGallery asset page was read. The 1873 Board report passage is quoted from LighthouseFriends; the corpus holds Light-House Board reports only from 1891, so it was not checked against the original. No source read names a hazard the light answered (the 'hazard to river traffic' phrasing was removed); the story states only the appropriation and the marking purpose. The 1838 Johnston raid and the Lossing quotation are LighthouseFriends' account; no newspaper or other primary was checked. The keepers' quarters date conflicts three ways: LighthouseFriends 1884 Victorian dwelling, Rowlett 1882 frame keeper's quarters, and the USLHS record (1848, Victorian, wood). The story states the LighthouseFriends/Rowlett conflict; the USLHS date is flagged here only. Restoration cost: Rowlett $1.1 million; LighthouseFriends $1.5 million federal and state; both stated. The 1915 Bulletin event is dated only by the volume year (May 9); no year is printed in the passage. Index entries in the 1912 Bulletin (Frederick Lawson, Sunken Rock) and the 1915 Commissioner list (Belden) are not used: the first is a different station, Sunken Rock. Brief's characteristic 'FW' and focal height 15 m differ from Rowlett's 52 ft (16 m) focal plane: the JSON uses Rowlett's height. Chesterfield Pearson is spelled 'Pearson' in LighthouseFriends and 'Pearsons' in the USLHS roster; the story uses the roster spelling for the roster and LighthouseFriends' for the narrative. Emma Diepolder: archive role laborer, LighthouseFriends keeper; the story uses both.
